summary: Pine Mountain lookout, Angeles NF, Los Angeles County: 1935 cabin on a 10 ft timber tower, burned in 1968 and not rebuilt. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin atop a 10-foot open timber tower
facts.status_note: Burned in 1968 and not rebuilt, per the register and 1968 newspaper items quoted on Forest Lookouts. No source describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Angeles National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1935 as the build year. The site was chosen after a seen-area survey completed in 1934.
Covina Argus item dated August 20, 1937 says work had started on a garage at the lookout (as quoted by Forest Lookouts).
Used for a Los Angeles County cloud seeding project for a time. The register gives only 'early to mid 1960's'; 1960 is the decade start, not a sourced date.
Burned in an August 1968 fire in the Fish Canyon area. The register files it as a 1968 arson fire and says the building was burned by 'hippies' and not rebuilt.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it an arson fire and says 'hippies' burned the building. The 1968 newspaper items quoted on Forest Lookouts describe a group of 'hippies' chased from the Fish Canyon cabins but do not tie that group to the tower. The story reports the register's account as the register's, not as settled fact.

notes_for_editor: Register and newspaper sources agree on the 1935 build and the 1968 burning, and the brief record matches them, so no corrections are proposed. Staffing ends 'by the late 1940s' per the register and is consistent with a 1968 item saying the tower had been abandoned for 20 years; no staffed_last event is written because the source gives no exact year. The cloud seeding use is recorded as an 'other' event dated 1960 (decade start only). The register's 'hippies' attribution is repeated with attribution and not endorsed; the Pasadena excerpt does not name a cause. Public access and current site condition are not described in any source read, so no access or visit facts are written. The Angeles Adventures lookouts page lists Pine Mountain, but its text was not read for site details. The brief id ends in '-2', which suggests a sibling record for another Pine Mountain. A rental listing says a Lake County Pine Mountain near Potter Valley was built in 1933 and used for fire detection until 1942; that is a different site and is not used here. No photos are listed: the register's newspaper images (dated March 29, 1934 and July 19, 1964) are credited but their image URLs were not captured.
